                         JOINT STIPULATION AND SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT

                 COME NOW the undersigned parties to the above entitled Case (“Stipulating Parties”) and
         present the following Joint Stipulation and Settlement Agreement (“Joint Stipulation”) for the
         Oklahoma Corporation Commission's (“Commission”) review and approval as their compromise
         and settlement of issues in this proceeding. The Stipulating Parties represent to the Commission
         that this Joint Stipulation represents a fair, just and reasonable settlement of the issues in this Case,
         that they believe the terms and conditions of the Joint Stipulation are in the public interest, and the
         Stipulating Parties request the Commission issue an Order adopting and approving this Joint
         Stipulation.
                 Effective with a Final Order approving all the elements of this Joint Stipulation, it is hereby
         stipulated and agreed by and between the Stipulating Parties as follows:


                                       I.      Jurisdiction of the Commission
                 The Stipulating Parties agree that the Commission has jurisdiction with respect to the issues
         presented in this proceeding by virtue of Article IX, §18 of the Oklahoma Constitution, 17 O.S. §
         152 et seq., 17 O.S. §286, the Commission’s Rules of Practice (OAC 165:5), and the Commission’s
         Electric Utility Rules (OAC 165:35).


                                II.     Recommendations of the Stipulating Parties
                 This Joint Stipulation represents a comprehensive settlement to become effective with the
         issuance of a Commission Order approving this Joint Stipulation (“Effective Date”).


         A. Approvals. The Parties recommend that the Commission approve the three OG&E–Alliance
             Site and Grid ESAs as special contracts under OAC 165:35-1-2 deemed tariffs under OAC
 CASE PUD 2026-000031 ENTRY NO. 149 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 09/09/2026 - PAGE 2 OF 9




            165:35-5-1(d), grant § 286(C) preapproval of the Rush Springs and High Spring CPAs with
            capacity costs recoverable through the FCA subject to annual prudence review, and approve
            the SRAC as proposed, subject to the following terms and conditions.

         B. Customer impact assessment. OG&E shall perform Customer Impact Assessments under the
            prescribed Base Case / What-If methodology. This Assessment shall be conducted in each
            general rate case conducted during the life of the contract. See Customer Impact Assessment
            (“Assessment”) to be supplemented as Exhibit A.

         C. Transmission. Google funds 100% of dedicated transmission and distribution infrastructure
            as CIAC. OG&E has identified no necessary regional or network upgrades as a direct result of
            the Google load as determined pursuant to the cost causation principles required by 17 O.S.
            Sections 900-906, and must notify the Commission and the Stipulating parties within 30 days
            if it later does. Upon an SPP determination of a regional or network upgrade as a result of the
            Google load as determined as previously stated, OG&E and Google will engage in good faith
            negotiations for how those costs should be handled, and OG&E will propose a methodology
            to the Commission in a future proceeding, which may be challenged by any party to the case.

         D. Cost allocation inputs. If CWIP is approved by the Commission to be recovered from
            customers, CWIP shall also be collected from Google.

         E. Revenue adequacy and billing minimums. OG&E shall provide to the Public Utility
            Division and the Oklahoma Attorney General a Highly Sensitive Confidential 12-month
            projection of minimum bill revenues per site and in aggregate within 90 days of a final order
            in this Case and update it annually until each site reaches full Contract Demand. Any cost
            component later moved into base rates becomes subject to the billing minimums.
            Supplemental Resource Administrative Charge (“SRAC”) revenues shall be separately
            tracked.

         F. Resource adequacy tracking. During the IRP process and pursuant to a protective order,
            OG&E shall provide Highly Sensitive Confidential information related to the portion of
            forecast requirement attributable to the XLPL Tariff customer class. Customers of this class
            will not be individually identified.

                                            III.    General Reservations

                The Stipulating Parties represent and agree that, except as may be specifically provided for
         herein to the following general reservations:
            A. Negotiated Settlement
                This Joint Stipulation represents a negotiated settlement for the purpose of compromising
         and resolving all issues raised in this Case.
            B. Authority to Execute
                Each of the undersigned affirmatively represents to the Commission that he or she has fully
         advised his or her respective client(s) that the execution of this Joint Stipulation constitutes a
         resolution of issues which were raised in this proceeding; that no promise, inducement or
         agreement not herein expressed has been made to any Stipulating Party; that this Joint Stipulation
         constitutes the entire agreement between and among the Stipulating Parties; and each of the
         undersigned affirmatively represents that he or she has full authority to execute this Joint
         Stipulation on behalf of his or her client(s).
            C. Joint Stipulation Represents a Balance and Compromise of Positions
                The Stipulating Parties stipulate and agree that the agreements contained in this Joint
         Stipulation have resulted from negotiations among the Stipulating Parties. The Stipulating Parties
         hereto specifically state and recognize that this Joint Stipulation represents a balancing of positions
         of each of the Stipulating Parties in consideration for the agreements and commitments made by
         the other Stipulating Parties in connection therewith. Therefore, in the event that the Commission
         does not approve and adopt all of the terms of this Joint Stipulation, this Joint Stipulation shall be
         void and of no force and effect, and no Stipulating Party shall be bound by the agreements or
         provisions contained herein. The Stipulating Parties agree that neither this Joint Stipulation nor
         any of the provisions hereof shall become effective unless and until the Commission shall have
         entered an Order approving all of the terms and provisions as agreed to by the parties to this Joint
         Stipulation.
            D. No Admissions Nor Waivers
                The Stipulating Parties agree and represent that the provisions of this Joint Stipulation are
         intended to relate only to the specific matters referred to herein, and by agreeing to this Joint
         Stipulation, no Stipulating Party waives any claim or right which it may otherwise have with
         respect to any matters not expressly provided for herein. Nothing contained herein shall constitute

         an admission by any Stipulating Party that any allegation or contention in this proceeding is true
         or valid or shall constitute a determination by the Commission as to the merits of any allegations
         or contentions made in this proceeding.
            E. No Precedential Value
                The Stipulating Parties agree that the provisions of this Joint Stipulation are the result of
         negotiations, and the terms and conditions of this Joint Stipulation are interdependent. The
         Stipulating Parties further agree and represent that neither this Joint Stipulation nor any
         Commission order approving the same shall constitute or be cited as precedent or deemed an
         admission by any Stipulating Party in any other proceeding except as necessary to enforce its terms
         before the Commission or any court of competent jurisdiction. The Commission’s decision, if it
         enters an order approving this Joint Stipulation, will be binding as to the matters decided regarding
         the issues described in this Joint Stipulation, but the decision will not be binding with respect to
         similar issues that might arise in future proceedings. A Stipulating Party’s support of this Joint
         Stipulation may differ from its position or testimony in other cases. To the extent there is a
         difference, the Stipulating Parties are not waiving their respective positions in other cases. Because
         this is a stipulated agreement, the Stipulating Parties are under no obligation to take the same
         position as set out in this Joint Stipulation in other dockets.
            F. Outstanding Discovery and Motions
                As between and among the Stipulating Parties, any pending requests for information or
         discovery and any motions that may be pending before the Commission or the Administrative Law
         Judge are hereby withdrawn.

                                                     EXHIBIT “A”
                    TO THE JOINT STIPULATION AND SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT
                                             CASE NO. PUD2026-000031
                                  CUSTOMER IMPACT REVIEW PROTOCOL


         3.1 Customer impact assessment. This set of principles shall be considered by OG&E in
         conducting Customer Impact Assessments (“Assessment”) in each general rate case conducted
         during the life of the Google ESAs. It is not binding on OG&E or other intervenors and meant to
         serve as a starting point for conducting a with and without Google analysis. The parties recognize
         that the XLPL case (PUD No. 2026-46) and future rate cases may provide additional guidance on
         these principles.
         3.2 Scope limitation. Cost-of-service allocation, the reasonableness of the calculated Customer Impact,
         and class rate design arising from the Assessment shall be adjudicated only in a general rate case or other
         proceeding as determined by the Commission.

         3.3 Methodology. Each Assessment shall compare:
             (a) Base Case — actual operations and costs;

             (b) What-If Case — the Base Case with the Google load removed, together with the accredited
             capacity and required capacity reserves associated with serving that load

         3.4 What if Case.     The Assessment must isolate and differentiate between Google-caused costs and
         independent system drivers. It must not attribute costs to Google for removal in the What If Case that are
         driven by independent factors, including but not limited to:

             A. Load growth in other customer classes,
             B. Fleet-wide environmental retirements,
             C. General system reliability or regional transmission investments that would be required regardless
                of Google's presence, and

         General system-wide cost increases. In assessing the shifting of demand and energy allocators, the analysis
         must account for these independent system variables to ensure that the What If case only removes costs
         Google directly causes.

         Any What if case needs to also include consideration of the benefits the Google load brings to existing
         customers and how the removal of those benefits also impacts the Assessment, while excluding non-
         qualifying benefits under Section 3.7.

         3.5 Generating Capacity and Price applied. The generating capacity removed in the What-If Case equals
         the accredited capacity and required capacity reserves (MW) required to serve the Google load, determined
         on the same accreditation basis SPP applied. Capacity removed shall be priced at the net cost of generation
         resources, expressed in $/kW-year, having a commercial operation date or contract start date on or after

         July 1, 2026—including owned generation, PPAs, CPAs, and other capacity contracts—and shall capture
         fixed capital and O&M costs, fuel and non-fuel variable costs, and market revenues. Average embedded
         cost of the total generation fleet shall not be used as the basis for determining the price of capacity required
         to serve Google that is removed in the What-If Case.

         3.6 Allocator effects. In assessing the effect of shifting demand and energy allocators, only the removal
         of the Google load shall be modeled. No other load, resource, or cost change shall be assumed.

         3.7 Exclusions. The Assessment shall not credit other economic effects, including job creation, taxes paid,
         or induced economic development. In addition, the Assessment shall not credit grid resilience or other
         reliability benefits.

         3.8 Burden. OG&E bears the burden of producing and supporting each Assessment along with underlying
         calculations and assumptions. All parties retain the right to review, contest, and offer alternative
         calculations in the rate case or other proceeding as determined by the Commission in which the customer
         impact amount is determined.

         3.9 Flexibility and Right to Contest. The methodologies and principles outlined herein represent a starting
         framework. All parties (including Google, OG&E, the PUD, and the Attorney General) explicitly retain
         their unrestricted right to advocate for alternative calculations, refinements, or different cost-of-service
         methodologies in future rate cases over the life of the service contracts.
